features.title: Define page functions
features.user_visible_behavior: A user, designer, or builder can understand what each major X-META Video page or surface is for before implementation begins.
verification: Read the interface design artifact completely.
Verify each app surface has a clear user goal and primary task.
Verify surfaces cover entry, project workspace, workflow canvas, node configuration, asset library, task status, generation history, export, auth, and workspace management.
Verify no page function implies backend, persistence, orchestration, connector, or AI execution behavior that is not implemented yet.
features.notes: Keep this as product/interface planning only; implementation belongs to later feature tasks.

features.title: Create the MVP screen inventory
features.user_visible_behavior: A user or builder can see the complete MVP screen list needed for comic drama, MV, and short-form video creation workflows.
verification: Review the screen inventory.
Verify every screen has a title, purpose, primary action, secondary actions, and empty/loading/error state notes.
Verify screens support comic drama, MV, and short-form video workflows without becoming a chat-first interface.
Verify screens map back to the product workflow in docs/PRODUCT.md.
features.notes: Include MVP screens first and clearly label future surfaces.

features.title: Design the information architecture
features.user_visible_behavior: A user can predict where to find projects, canvas tools, node settings, generated assets, task status, history, and exports.
verification: Review the navigation and information architecture model.
Verify every screen has documented entry points, exit points, and no dead ends.
Verify primary navigation, workspace navigation, contextual panels, and modal or drawer behavior are documented.
Verify node configuration, asset reuse, retry, and export paths are easy to trace.
Verify the information architecture does not conflict with docs/ARCHITECTURE.md layer boundaries.
features.notes: The web app owns navigation and local UI state; backend state ownership should remain clearly labeled.

features.title: Sketch core UI layouts
features.user_visible_behavior: A user can see rough layout direction for the app shell, node canvas, node inspector, asset drawer, task status, history, and export surfaces.
verification: Review the rough sketches or wireframe descriptions.
Verify each sketch labels visible regions, primary interactions, and status feedback.
Verify the canvas remains the central workspace surface for creative production.
Verify sketches use familiar web app patterns and avoid unrelated chat, generic dashboard, or marketing-page layouts.
features.notes: Use shadcn/ui and UI TripleD-inspired visual direction where applicable, but keep sketches implementation-agnostic.

features.title: Write wireframing guidelines
features.user_visible_behavior: A designer or builder can produce consistent wireframes for future node, asset, project-management, and generation-status screens.
verification: Review the wireframing guidelines.
Verify spacing, panel hierarchy, toolbar behavior, node cards, inspector patterns, asset cards, tables, and status regions are defined.
Verify guidelines cover script, storyboard, character, scene, prop, image composition, audio, video, 9-grid storyboard, and export node surfaces.
Verify guidelines call out reusable components and layout patterns instead of one-off page designs.
features.notes: Keep guidance concise and reusable across future feature files.

features.title: Define responsive states
features.user_visible_behavior: A user can understand how the planned interface works on desktop, tablet, and mobile without losing primary actions or context.
verification: Review responsive state definitions.
Verify desktop, tablet, and mobile layouts are described for the app shell, canvas, inspectors, asset panels, task status, and export flow.
Verify canvas controls, node settings, asset reuse, and task feedback remain reachable.
Verify mobile constraints are honest about limited canvas editing and provide a clear review or lightweight-edit path.
features.notes: Prefer clear responsive behavior over trying to preserve every desktop panel at small widths.

features.title: Document accessibility requirements
features.user_visible_behavior: A keyboard or assistive-technology user has a planned path through navigation, canvas controls, node settings, generated assets, and task feedback.
verification: Review accessibility requirements.
Verify keyboard order, focus states, labels, landmarks, contrast, and reduced-motion expectations are documented.
Verify node selection, edge editing, inspector controls, asset selection, and export settings have accessible interaction alternatives.
Verify async task status is communicated without relying only on color, motion, or spatial position.
features.notes: Document design requirements only; implementation and automated accessibility testing belong to build tasks.

features.title: Prepare implementation handoff artifacts
features.user_visible_behavior: A builder can start the next implementation feature with clear design scope, acceptance criteria, page maps, and known non-goals.
verification: Review the handoff package.
Verify it includes page-function map, screen inventory, information architecture notes, sketches or wireframe descriptions, reusable wireframe rules, responsive states, and accessibility notes.
Verify implementation boundaries and missing backend, connector, orchestration, audit, and persistence capabilities are labeled honestly.
Verify Feature 3 can reference these artifacts without relying on chat history.
features.notes: Handoff should be stored in repository artifacts when the feature is implemented.
